Procurement asked me to share a light snapshot of expected usage so they can start sizing reserved capacity and determine whether we should request a committed discount for the pilot. Attached is a short PDF with our UX flows and expected Q4 peaks.

High level forecast (pilot):

- Burst events (demo days): up to 3x weekday peak for 2 hours
- Embeddings job: nightly batch (00:30 PT) — ~6M tokens/day

Questions for you:
1) For the weekday profile above, what dedicated slot commitment would you recommend to keep 95p token latency < 250ms?
2) Can we schedule a quick call with infra and finance to align on commit windows and discount thresholds?

I attached acme_capacity_requirements_v1.pdf — it has a short appendix with token distribution by route.

—Emily

On Thu, Oct 17, 2029 at 07:12 AM laura_bennett@redwood.com wrote:
> Looping finance and pricing in early. A couple of constraints from our side:
> - Minimum commercial commit for dedicated pricing starts at a 3-month monthly-committed baseline.
> - To approve the pilot discount band, we need a burn range (low/typical/high) and a committed slot count for the pilot weeks.

Team — I ran the numbers against Emily’s appendix and Aditya’s baseline. Notes below and attached a small calc (capacity_estimate_v3.xlsx).

Capacity sizing & risk:
- Baseline recommendation: 4 x A100-eq reserved slots (weekday 08:00–20:00 PT). This aligns with 95p token latency target under steady-state.
- Burst: keep 3 x transient slots available via burst credits (we can allocate burst capacity per-deal for the first 8 weeks).
- Embeddings: schedule to non-peak window or run on dedicated 1-slot nightly; cost-optimal to use burst credits unless they commit to a nightly reserved slot.

Ops guardrails (short):
- Canary: route 10% of traffic to a lower-cost quantized variant for first 48 hours post-cutover and monitor P50/P95 latency + perplexity drift. I attached canary_config_snippet.txt with the threshold triggers.
- Fallbacks: auto-route to hosted-compatible smaller instance if reserved pool drops below 3 slots; SLAs are tied to committed slots only, we should document fallbacks in the SOW.

Rough cost (net):
- No discount: est $X/month (see sheet)
- 10% commit discount: est $X1/month
- 20% commit discount: est $X2/month

Laura/Kim — please confirm what discount breakpoints we should price in the sheet for procurement. Emily — if you can confirm expected pilot duration (weeks) and any demo cadence, I’ll finalize the burn range.

—Ben
Principal Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference
